findings.highlight: smaller countries
findings.evidenceJa: 様々な小王国
findings.governingReading: After imperial protection ends, her country rapidly fragments into various small kingdoms.
findings.explanation: Countries removes the monarchical political structure and various becomes only a comparative size.

findings.highlight: felt the same air from the girl as he did from his king
findings.evidenceJa: 主君と同じ物を感じた
findings.governingReading: The old knight senses in the girl the same essential quality he knows in his lord.
findings.explanation: Felt the same air from is Japanese-shaped English that leaves the decisive perceived quality obscure.

findings.highlight: King born of England
findings.evidenceJa: ブリテンの王
findings.governingReading: The golden inscription names the rightful king of Britain.
findings.explanation: The borrowed Arthurian wording substitutes England for Britain, changing the polity named by this script.

findings.highlight: someone who kills everyone to protect everyone
findings.evidenceJa: 一番多くみんなを殺す存在
findings.governingReading: The king protects everyone by becoming the person who kills more people than anyone else.
findings.explanation: Kills everyone turns the paradox of bearing the greatest lethal burden into indiscriminate total slaughter.

findings.highlight: No one will care about the king’s appearance or even notice it
findings.evidenceJa: 王の風貌など誰も気にかけず
findings.governingReading: If she functions as an excellent king, no one will concern themselves with her appearance.
findings.explanation: Or even notice it asserts that her sex goes unnoticed, although the next line expressly allows that some may recognize it.

findings.highlight: praised their master’s immortality as divine
findings.evidenceJa: 主君の不死性を神秘と讃えあげた
findings.governingReading: Most knights exalt the Mystery of their lord’s unaging state.
findings.explanation: Divine introduces godliness and loses the work’s technical and atmospheric category of Mystery.

findings.highlight: a dragon in human form
findings.evidenceJa: 竜の化身
findings.governingReading: The king’s body is celebrated as the incarnation or avatar of a dragon.
findings.explanation: Dragon in human form describes a disguised dragon and narrows the incarnation claim.

findings.highlight: Resting her body in the wind
findings.evidenceJa: 風に身を任せて
findings.governingReading: Before dawn, she gives herself over to the wind beneath the indigo sky.
findings.explanation: Resting her body is stiff and changes passive surrender to the wind into physical repose.

findings.highlight: the sword that selected her fate
findings.evidenceJa: 運命を決定した剣
findings.governingReading: The sword determines the course of her fate.
findings.explanation: Selected her fate suggests choosing among possible fates rather than decisively fixing it.

findings.highlight: How did she lose
findings.evidenceJa: 何処に、失ってしまった
findings.governingReading: The dream closes by asking where she could have lost such a celebrated sword.
findings.explanation: How replaces the explicit mystery of where the sword was lost with a question about the manner of its loss.

findings.highlight: I guess I fell asleep after coming back to my room
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーを看ながら眠ってしまった
findings.governingReading: Unable to decide, Shirou falls asleep while watching over Saber.
findings.explanation: The English omits that he remained at Saber’s bedside, weakening the continuity of his care and the setting of the awakening.

findings.highlight: Saber’s true identity that was hidden
findings.evidenceJa: 不確かだったセイバーの正体
findings.governingReading: Saber’s identity had remained uncertain to Shirou.
findings.explanation: Hidden asserts concealment by an agent and changes his incomplete acceptance into a secret deliberately kept from him.

findings.highlight: I can’t change my attitude, attitude
findings.evidenceJa: 態度を変える事なんて出来ない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot change how he treats Saber because of the identity he has learned.
findings.explanation: Attitude is duplicated at the center of the relationship statement.

findings.highlight: it suited her
findings.evidenceJa: 似合ってたな、セイバー
findings.governingReading: Shirou addresses Saber by name as he says the sword suited her.
findings.explanation: The English turns an intimate spoken address into detached third-person narration.

findings.highlight: I take a deep breath
findings.evidenceJa: 大きく息を吐いて
findings.governingReading: Shirou lets out a long, heavy breath before reaching for his sweating forehead.
findings.explanation: Take a deep breath reverses exhalation into inhalation and loses the sighing release.

findings.highlight: my sweaty face
findings.evidenceJa: 汗まみれの額
findings.governingReading: Shirou reaches toward his sweat-soaked forehead.
findings.explanation: Face broadens the specific body part immediately named and touched.

findings.highlight: How selfish of me
findings.evidenceJa: 都合のいい事
findings.governingReading: Shirou violently rejects his own self-serving hope that Saber may recover without a decision.
findings.explanation: Selfish recasts wishful convenience as a broader moral indictment.

findings.highlight: I have to make a decision before she does
findings.evidenceJa: それまでに、俺はどちらを取るか決断
findings.governingReading: Shirou must choose between the two options before Saber wakes.
findings.explanation: Before she does grammatically makes Saber the person who makes a decision, reversing the understood event.

findings.highlight: There’s no energy in the house, and it feels like it’s abandoned
findings.evidenceJa: 家には活気がなく、廊下は廃墟のよう
findings.governingReading: The house lacks vitality and the corridor specifically looks like a ruin until Shirou corrects the impression as his own depression.
findings.explanation: The English makes the whole house feel literally abandoned and removes the corridor’s ruin simile.

findings.highlight: He must have been shooting arrows until now
findings.evidenceJa: 先ほどまで弓を引いていたのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou initially sees only that Archer appears to have been drawing his bow.
findings.explanation: The English asserts he was shooting arrows, immediately contradicting the reveal that he used none.

findings.highlight: Don’t shoot bows
findings.evidenceJa: 弓なんて引くな
findings.governingReading: Shirou tells Archer not to draw a bow in someone else’s yard.
findings.explanation: Shoot bows treats the bow itself as the projectile and corrupts the action.

findings.highlight: Archer isn’t using any arrows, but only pulling his bow
findings.evidenceJa: 矢を使わず、ただ弓を引いていた
findings.governingReading: Archer is simply drawing the bow without using arrows.
findings.explanation: The sentence stacks but after an earlier but, producing malformed contrast.

findings.highlight: curls his lips offensively
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌味に口元をつりあげる
findings.governingReading: Archer curls his lips into a sarcastic or needling smile.
findings.explanation: Offensively describes Shirou’s reaction rather than the specific sarcasm carried by Archer’s expression.

findings.highlight: concept called ‘follow-through’
findings.evidenceJa: 残心、という言葉
findings.governingReading: Archer introduces the named kyudo concept zanshin, which the ensuing dialogue defines as a mental disposition toward a completed act.
findings.explanation: Follow-through substitutes a generic mechanical term before the scene explains its distinct mental meaning.

findings.highlight: The time you have after you take your shot
findings.evidenceJa: 事を済ませた後に保つ間
findings.governingReading: Archer first defines zanshin broadly as the interval maintained after completing an act, then compares their archery.
findings.explanation: After you take your shot prematurely narrows the definition and loses its planned application to Shirou’s moral choice.

findings.highlight: if you think the arrow will hit, it will hit the target
findings.evidenceJa: 当たると思えば当たっている
findings.governingReading: For the archer, the hit is already settled in the pre-release image; zanshin does not inspect whether it occurred.
findings.explanation: The English makes thinking cause the future hit, turning Archer’s account of prior commitment into a universal-sounding law of accuracy.

findings.highlight: Well, you hit the target every time
findings.evidenceJa: 少なくとも、おまえは百発百中だろう
findings.governingReading: Archer says that Shirou, at least, is presumably unerring.
findings.explanation: The English removes both the limiting at least and the inferential tone, presenting his accuracy as flat fact.

findings.highlight: see through this thing until the end
findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで見届けろ
findings.governingReading: Shirou takes Archer to mean that he must witness the result through to the end.
findings.explanation: See through this thing is unnatural and can mean completing or penetrating it rather than remaining to witness the consequence.

findings.highlight: all I can do is see through what happens
findings.evidenceJa: 見届けるしか出来ない
findings.governingReading: Shirou angrily asks whether he can do nothing but witness whatever his choice does to Saber.
findings.explanation: See through what happens again obscures witnessing and accepting the consequence.

findings.highlight: did not intend to use her Noble Phantasm until the very end
findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで宝具を使う気はなかった
findings.governingReading: Archer cautiously infers that Saber intended never to use her Noble Phantasm throughout the fight.
findings.explanation: Until the very end can mean that she planned to use it at the final moment, reversing the point that protecting Shirou made her abandon a settled refusal.

findings.highlight: honest sincerity
findings.evidenceJa: 事実を告げる誠実さ
findings.governingReading: Archer’s voice contains only the sincerity of stating the fact, with his usual sarcasm gone.
findings.explanation: Honest sincerity is redundant and drops the important link between his unadorned tone and the factual warning.
